desc: This is the hardest artifact in the domain: an executed federal research instrument binding the United States Army to a company that publicly claimed custody of material from a vehicle of unknown origin. Signed on 10 October 2019 by Jeffery Langhout, Director of the Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center, and Kari DeLonge for TTSA, and announced on 17 October 2019, it named Bean Soave and Dr. Joseph Cannon as government principal investigators and Luis Elizondo, as TTSA's Director of Global Security & Special Programs, as the collaborator principal investigator. The stated research areas are 'inertial mass reduction, mechanical/structural meta materials, electromagnetic meta material wave guides, quantum physics, quantum communications, and beamed energy propulsion', with 'Active Camouflage' and 'Directed Photon Projection' named as applications. The document runs to 30 September 2023 with annual intellectual property reviews and estimates the value of TTSA's participation at $1 million in in-kind contributions; the Army provided laboratories, expertise and resources reported at not less than $750,000 in value. The Army released the agreement itself on 18 October 2019 but on 21 February 2020 denied in full a FOIA request for the associated correspondence — twenty-nine emails, one hundred pages — under exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5). No technical results have ever been published.

claims.source: https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/army/TTSA-ARMY-CRADA.pdf (26 pages, released by U.S. Army CCDC GVSC to The Black Vault, October 2019)
claims.text: The executed agreement is CRADA Number 19-15, titled 'Novel & Emerging Technology Exploitation (NETE),' between To The Stars Academy of Arts and Science, Inc. and the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Ground Vehicle Systems Center, 6501 E. 11 Mile Road, Warren, MI 48397-5000.

The Collaborator Principal Investigator and preferred point of contact named in the CRADA is Luis Elizondo, 'Director of Global Security and Special Programs,' at 315 South Coast Hwy 101, Ste. U-38, Encinitas, CA 92024.

The Government Principal Investigators named in the CRADA are Ben Soave and Dr. Joseph Cannon of Ground Vehicle Survivability and Protection (GVSP), MS 263b; the Office of Research and Technology Applications representative is Andrea Simon; Government legal counsel is Christina Dellmore, Chief, Intellectual Property Law Division, US Army TACOM LCMC.
Collaborator legal counsel named in the CRADA is Heidy Vaquerano, Esq., of Wolf, Rifkin, Shapiro, Schulman & Rabkin, LLP, 11400 W. Olympic Boulevard, 9th Floor, Los Angeles, CA 90064.

The CRADA Joint Work Plan states: 'The Government is interested in a variety of the Collaborator's technologies, such as, but not limited to inertial mass reduction, mechanical/structural metamaterials, electromagnetic metamaterial wave guides, quantum physics, quantum communications, and beamed energy propulsion.'

The CRADA obligates the Collaborator to 'Provide the agreed upon materiel technologies for USG testing and evaluation,' specifically including 'Metamaterial: Samples of mechanical and EM sensitive metamaterial collected, obtained, or developed as part of its Field Operations,' along with written material analysis data and quantum communication research.

Article 4.2 of the CRADA provides that the agreement 'will automatically expire sixty (60) months from the Effective Date of this CRADA, unless modified per Article 4.6,' and Article 4.3 provides that it 'enters into force as of the date it is signed by the last authorized representative of the Parties'; Section III repeats the sixty-month expiration and provides that rights and responsibilities survive completion, expiration or termination.

Information exchanged under the CRADA is protected in accordance with 15 U.S.C. section 3710a(c)(7), and licenses to CRADA inventions are granted in accordance with 15 U.S.C. section 3710a(b)(2); the Collaborator's option to choose an exclusive license must be requested within six months of being notified of a CRADA Invention, subject to the Government retaining a nonexclusive, transferable license.

The same SEC filing states that laboratory testing planned under the ADAM Research Project 'was paused and will resume at some future date when laboratories resume' operations.

dossier.denialPosture: The Army's posture is that CRADA 19-15 is unremarkable technology transfer, that a CRADA is not an endorsement mechanism, that the arrangement is directly comparable to the Army's fuel-cell CRADA with General Motors, and that the origin of the materials is 'immaterial' to the Army's interest. That posture sits badly against the Joint Work Plan's explicit interest in inertial mass reduction and beamed energy propulsion, and against DoD's later invocation of national-defense and foreign-policy FOIA exemptions to withhold records about an agreement it publicly characterized as routine and unclassified.
dossier.narrative:
On 17 October 2019 To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science issued a press release announcing a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command to develop enhanced capabilities for Army ground vehicles. The release was thin. The Army was not. Doug Halleaux, public affairs officer for CCDC's Ground Vehicle Systems Center, gave John Greenewald of The Black Vault the executed agreement, twenty-six pages, redacted only for phone numbers.

The document is CRADA No. 19-15, 'Novel & Emerging Technology Exploitation (NETE),' between TTSA and CCDC Ground Vehicle Systems Center, 6501 E. 11 Mile Road, Warren, Michigan. The named administrators matter. On the Government side the principal investigators are Ben Soave and Dr. Joseph Cannon, both of Ground Vehicle Survivability and Protection, mail stop 263b. The ORTA representative is Andrea Simon; Government legal counsel is Christina Dellmore, Chief of the Intellectual Property Law Division at US Army TACOM LCMC. On the Collaborator side, the principal investigator and preferred contact is Luis Elizondo, 'Director of Global Security and Special Programs,' Encinitas, California. Collaborator legal counsel is Heidy Vaquerano, Esq., of Wolf, Rifkin, Shapiro, Schulman & Rabkin, LLP, Los Angeles.

The Joint Work Plan is where the agreement stops sounding like armor research. The Government's stated interests are 'a variety of the Collaborator's technologies, such as, but not limited to inertial mass reduction, mechanical/structural metamaterials, electromagnetic metamaterial wave guides, quantum physics, quantum communications, and beamed energy propulsion.' The Collaborator's deliverables include, verbatim, 'Metamaterial: Samples of mechanical and EM sensitive metamaterial collected, obtained, or developed as part of its Field Operations,' plus written material analysis and quantum-communication research. 'Field Operations' is the operative euphemism; the CRADA does not define provenance, and the Army made a point of saying provenance was irrelevant to it.

The legal architecture is standard Federal Technology Transfer Act plumbing put to non-standard use. Information exchanged is protected under 15 U.S.C. section 3710a(c)(7), and every page carries a marking legend invoking it. Licenses to CRADA inventions run under 15 U.S.C. section 3710a(b)(2), with the Collaborator holding an option for an exclusive license that must be requested within six months of notification of an invention. The agreement automatically expires sixty months from the effective date under Article 4.2, and enters force on the date signed by the last authorized representative under Article 4.3.

TTSA's own SEC filings supply the numbers the CRADA does not. In its Regulation A offering circular the company states that on 10 October 2019 it entered into the CRADA with CCDC, that 'the purpose of the CRADA is to advance developments in material science (including testing of the metamaterials), space-time metric engineering, quantum physics, beamed energy propulsion and active camouflage,' that the parties bear their own costs, that the total value of anticipated U.S. Government resources including personnel, services, intellectual property, facilities, equipment and reporting is 'estimated at $750,000,' that the total value of the company's participation is 'estimated at $1,000,000,' and that the agreement is terminable by mutual consent or unilaterally on thirty days' notice.

The same filing describes where the material came from. The ADAM Research Project, Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials, launched in July 2018, and 'within one year this division acquired a collection of material samples reported to come from advanced vehicles of unknown origin from all over the world.' In July 2019 the company 'purchased multiple pieces of metamaterials and an archive of initial analysis and research.' Elsewhere TTSA states flatly to the SEC: 'The exotic materials that were purchased come from unidentified aerial phenomenon and are anomalous in that they have a structure and composition that we believe are unknown to any existing commercial or military application.' By November 2019, per the filing, ETI had performed analysis pursuant to the SOW-MSSA showing 'a unique physical structure unknown to any past or current commercial or military application.' The filing also records that planned ADAM laboratory testing 'was paused.'

The Army's public framing was deliberately deflationary. Halleaux told The Black Vault that 'the Army is providing the expertise and facilities to analyze the materials, and TTSA is providing the materials themselves; both parties receive the results of the analysis,' and that 'just as there is no financial compensation to TTSA for the use of the materials, there is no financial compensation to the Army for the use of the facilities.' On provenance he was explicit: 'the Army's interest is in the potential for novel materials and exploring the edges of materials science, any speculation as to their origin is (pardon the pun) immaterial.' He also stressed that a CRADA is not an endorsement, offering the Army's fuel-cell CRADA with General Motors as the comparison.

Then the record closed. Individuals who had custody of pieces of the metamaterial before TTSA acquired them were placed under non-disclosure agreements; The Black Vault reached one such person, who declined comment citing an NDA. Some of the material was described in SEC filings as being 'on loan.' The Department of Defense invoked FOIA exemptions covering national defense and foreign policy to withhold CRADA-related documents. It took until October 2024, five years after execution and at the natural end of the sixty-month term, before the Army agreed to a rolling release under FOIA case FA-24-0006, with the first package released on 23 October 2024.

The analytic point for the board is the instrument, not the rock. A CRADA requires no appropriation, no competition, no contract file and no reportable obligation, and carries a statutory information shield. It creates a lawful, low-visibility conduit for moving materials of undeclared origin into a federal laboratory and moving analysis and invention rights back out, with the collaborator holding a first option on exclusive rights to anything invented. Whatever the metamaterial turns out to be, CRADA 19-15 is the working proof that the channel exists, is routine, and is FOIA-resistant by design.

What tests did the Army actually perform, what did they find, and what does the close-out report say?

Are there other CRADAs between federal laboratories and private parties covering material of undeclared or anomalous provenance, and can they be enumerated through ORTA records?
What happened to the physical samples at expiration of the sixty-month term: returned, retained, consumed in testing, or transferred?
Who are the individuals under NDA to TTSA regarding provenance, and what does the NDA prohibit?
dossier.whatItIs: Cooperative Research and Development Agreement No. 19-15, titled 'Novel & Emerging Technology Exploitation (NETE),' between To The Stars Academy of Arts and Science, Inc. and the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Ground Vehicle Systems Center at the Detroit Arsenal, Warren, Michigan. Executed under 15 U.S.C. section 3710a with a term of sixty months from the effective date, it committed TTSA to provide the Army with samples of metamaterial 'collected, obtained, or developed as part of its Field Operations' and the Army to provide laboratories, expertise and analysis, with no exchange of funds in either direction. TTSA's principal investigator of record was Luis Elizondo.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the only publicly released, signed U.S. Government instrument in which a federal laboratory agrees to characterize material that the counterparty represented, in filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission, as coming from unidentified aerial phenomena. That makes it the board's hardest documentary bridge between the alleged recovery-and-exploitation enterprise and the ordinary federal technology-transfer system. The Joint Work Plan names the Government's actual interests, and the list is not generic materials science: 'inertial mass reduction, mechanical/structural metamaterials, electromagnetic metamaterial wave guides, quantum physics, quantum communications, and beamed energy propulsion.' Inertial mass reduction is not a ground-vehicle survivability requirement. The Collaborator principal investigator is Luis Elizondo, the former Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence official associated with AATIP who left DoD in 2017 alleging excessive secrecy, meaning the same individual who publicly accused the Pentagon of concealment is, two years later, the named point of contact delivering anomalous material back into an Army laboratory under an agreement whose supporting records the Department of Defense then withheld under national-defense FOIA exemptions. Finally, the CRADA form itself is the point: it moves technology and creates invention rights without appropriated funds, without a contract, without competition and without a reportable obligation, and it carries a statutory information shield. It is a legal channel for moving exploitable material into and out of the Government that leaves almost no financial footprint.
